findings.claim: ADR-026 names `src/sec10k/boilerplate.py::_demo` as an "Enforced by" artifact, but the new module is the only sec10k module with a `_demo` that was not added to the CI unit-tests job, so nothing ever runs it.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:28-32 runs `python3 -m src.sec10k.{test_eval_adapter,normalize,segment,validate,web.view}` and `evals.metrics --self-check`; `src.sec10k.boilerplate` is absent. `.githooks/pre-commit` runs only `evals.run --suite fast`, and `.claude/hooks/post-edit-invariant.sh` only `--suite invariant`. ADR-026 line 9 and specs/decisions/INDEX.md:33 both cite the self-check as enforcement. Measured consequence: four mutations are caught ONLY by `_demo` and are green on the whole gate - MIN_REPEATS 8->20, MIN_SPREAD 0.70->0.95, PAGE_DIGITS 3->4, and strip_chrome no-op (see R2).
findings.repro: grep -n 'src.sec10k' .github/workflows/ci.yml   # boilerplate missing; then `sed -i '' 's/PAGE_DIGITS = 3/PAGE_DIGITS = 4/' src/sec10k/boilerplate.py && python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant && python3 -m evals.run --suite fast` -> 33/33 and 74/74 green, while `python3 -m src.sec10k.boilerplate` exits 1
findings.acceptance: `- run: python3 -m src.sec10k.boilerplate` added to the ci.yml unit-tests job (or the ADR's "Enforced by" line stops claiming the self-check), so at least one automated gate goes red when `_demo` does.

findings.claim: `strip_chrome()` - the "stripped run is reconstructible" half of the S6 acceptance criterion - has zero eval-case coverage: replacing its whole body with `return text[start:end]` (a total no-op that strips nothing) leaves invariant 33/33, fast 74/74 and the adapter self-check 16/16 green.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/boilerplate.py:124-142. No committed case calls `strip_chrome`: `grep -rn strip_chrome evals/` returns only provenance prose in evals/adversarial/*.json. The adapter's three new check types (`boilerplate`, `boilerplate_spans_sane`, `offsets_invariant_under_exclusion`, src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py:205-266) all read `result["boilerplate"]` spans and never derive the stripped view. Combined with R1, the function is unguarded by anything that runs.
findings.repro: Insert `return text[start:len(text) if end is None else end]` as the first line of `strip_chrome` in src/sec10k/boilerplate.py, then `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant --no-report; python3 -m evals.run --suite fast --no-report; python3 -m src.sec10k.test_eval_adapter` -> 33/33, 74/74, 16/16 all green (only `python3 -m src.sec10k.boilerplate` goes red).
findings.acceptance: A committed case (fast or invariant) that asserts the stripped view on a real fixture - e.g. that `strip_chrome(normalized_text, boilerplate)` on msft-2013 no longer contains 'Table of Contents', is exactly 2,002 chars shorter, and that `normalized_text[start:end]` still reconstructs the original run - and that goes red under the no-op mutation.

findings.claim: `boilerplate-txt-chrome`'s dash-rule `max: 0` check is vacuous - its `value` string does not exist in ge-1994's normalized_text, so it selects zero runs no matter what the detector does, and the provenance's "measured" CV/spread for it belong to a different string.
findings.evidence: evals/adversarial/boilerplate-txt-chrome.json:79-82 asserts `{"value": "- " + 69 dashes (len 70), "max": 0}` and its provenance says "The 70-dash rule line occurs 37x at CV 0.82, spread 0.66: it is arguably chrome and is deliberately NOT detected (ADR-026 f1), and this check pins that as a decision". Measured on ge-1994 normalized_text: that exact 70-char line occurs **0** times; the real rule line is `'- ' + 75 dashes` (77 chars), occurs 37x, CV 0.82, spread 0.66. ADR-026 f1:248 repeats the same figures. The check therefore pins nothing.
findings.repro: python3 -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,os.getcwd());from src.sec10k.normalize import select_and_normalize;from src.sec10k.boilerplate import _lines;from pathlib import Path;t=select_and_normalize(Path('evals/fixtures/ge-1994/filing.txt').read_bytes().decode())[0];v='- '+'-'*69;print(sum(1 for x in _lines(t) if x[2]==v), sum(1 for x in _lines(t) if x[2]=='- '+'-'*75))" -> `0 37`. Then set `MAX_GAP_CV = 0.85` and `MIN_SPREAD = 0.60`: ge-1994 chrome goes 392 -> 429 spans (the 37 dash lines become `running_head`) and `boilerplate-txt-chrome` still PASSES.
findings.acceptance: The check's `value` is the string that actually occurs (`'- ' + 75*'-'`), and loosening MAX_GAP_CV/MIN_SPREAD until that line is classified as chrome turns `boilerplate-txt-chrome` red.

findings.claim: The MIN_SPREAD threshold's value is not pinned by any eval case: lowering it 0.70 -> 0.40 keeps every suite green while adding 73 false `running_head` spans on jpm-2024 - exactly the section-level heads ADR-026 c3/f1 say the gate exists to reject and that c6's "zero false positives" depends on.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/boilerplate.py:47. With `MIN_SPREAD = 0.40`, jpm-2024 `find_chrome` returns 653 spans instead of 572, including 73x `'Notes to consolidated financial statements'` (CV 0.28, spread 0.42) and 8x `'2024'` (spread 0.64, the ADR's own nearest non-chrome data point). No committed case runs jpm-2024 (or any fixture with a section-level running head) with `exclude_boilerplate`; the near-miss corpus is msft-2013 + cvx-2015 only, whose worst near-miss spreads are 0.35/0.26. MAX_GAP_CV has the same hole: 0.60 -> 0.80 leaves all four cases and `_demo` green.
findings.repro: sed -i '' 's/MIN_SPREAD = 0.70/MIN_SPREAD = 0.40/' src/sec10k/boilerplate.py && python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant --no-report && python3 -m evals.run --suite fast --no-report && python3 -m src.sec10k.boilerplate  -> 33/33, 74/74, self-check ok (all green)
findings.acceptance: A case running jpm-2024 (or nvda-2024) with `exclude_boilerplate: true` and `{"value": "Notes to consolidated financial statements", "max": 0}` / `{"value": "NVIDIA Corporation and Subsidiaries", "max": 0}`, which goes red at MIN_SPREAD 0.40 and green at 0.70.

findings.claim: The "above" half of the page-number adjacency rule is unexercised: dropping it silently halves detected page numbers on jpm-2024 (286 -> 143) with every suite and the module self-check still green.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/boilerplate.py:117 `if kinds.get(neighbour(i, -1)) or kinds.get(neighbour(i, 1)):` implements ADR-026 b's "the nearest non-blank line above **or** below". Mutating it to `if kinds.get(neighbour(i, 1)):` (below only) changes nothing on msft-2013 (94) or ge-1994 (392) - the only two fixtures the new cases run - but jpm-2024's `page_number` count drops from 286 to 143, i.e. every page whose footer number sits *under* the running head is lost. `boilerplate._demo` is also blind to it (its synthetic pages happen to have a head below every number), so it stays green too.
findings.repro: Replace `if kinds.get(neighbour(i, -1)) or kinds.get(neighbour(i, 1)):` with `if kinds.get(neighbour(i, 1)):` in src/sec10k/boilerplate.py, then `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant --no-report; python3 -m evals.run --suite fast --no-report; python3 -m src.sec10k.boilerplate`   # 33/33, 74/74, self-check ok
findings.acceptance: A case (fixture or `_demo`) whose page numbers are adjacent to chrome only from above - e.g. a jpm-2024 `{"kind":"page_number","min":280}` check, or a `_demo` block with a trailing footer under the head - which goes red under the below-only mutation.

findings.claim: Three figures written in the voice of a measurement do not reproduce: cvx-2015's "2,063 bare-number lines" (actual 2,045), "518 distinct line texts repeating 3+ times" (actual 521), and the shipped code's "24 real EDGAR filings" corpus size (actual 28, as ADR-026 c itself says).
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/boilerplate.py:31 and :39-41; specs/decisions/ADR-026-boilerplate-chrome-exclusion.md:62, :266; evals/adversarial/boilerplate-near-miss.json provenance ("measured 2026-08-22 ... 518 distinct line texts repeating 3+ times ... 2,063 lines that consist of nothing but a bare number"). Measured on cvx-2015 normalized_text (417,523 chars, 21,845 lines, which do reproduce): lines whose stripped text `.isdigit()` = **2,045**; distinct stripped line texts with count >= 3 = **521**. No alternate definition reaches 2,063 or 518 (1-3 digits: 1,795; digits with parens: 2,550; count>=2: 1,122; count>=4: 279). Fixture count: 38 dirs - 9 self-created mutants - `repo_hygiene` = **28**, contradicting boilerplate.py's "24".
findings.repro: python3 -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,os.getcwd());from src.sec10k.normalize import select_and_normalize;from pathlib import Path;import collections;t=select_and_normalize(Path('evals/fixtures/cvx-2015/filing.htm').read_bytes().decode())[0];L=[l.strip() for l in t.split(chr(10))];c=collections.Counter(x for x in L if x);print(sum(1 for x in L if x.isdigit()), sum(1 for v,n in c.items() if n>=3))" -> `2045 521`
findings.acceptance: The three numbers are corrected to what the audit script in ADR-026 c6 prints (2,045 / 521 / 28), or each is relabelled with the definition under which it reproduces.

findings.claim: ADR-026's enforcement map (d and the g table) misstates which case asserts what: it claims the invariant-suite case covers both an HTML and a txt fixture, and credits `boilerplate-chrome-detected` with a flag-OFF assertion it does not contain.
findings.evidence: ADR-026 d:188-190 "asserts it as an **invariant-suite** case on both an HTML fixture that fires and a txt fixture that fires" and g:279 "`boilerplate-offsets-invariant` | **invariant** | msft-2013 **and ge-1994**". The committed evals/adversarial/boilerplate-offsets-invariant.json runs msft-2013 only, and its own provenance says the opposite: "The txt-era counterpart runs in the fast suite as boilerplate-txt-chrome's offsets_invariant_under_exclusion check." So the invariant suite has no txt-era offset-invariance coverage. g:276 also credits `boilerplate-chrome-detected` with "with the flag OFF the envelope carries no `boilerplate` key at all" - that case runs with `exclude_boilerplate: true` and has no such check (the OFF assertion lives only in `offsets_invariant_under_exclusion`, eval_adapter.py:263), and g:277 attributes msft-2013's `Total`/`PART II`/`Item 8` near-miss checks to `boilerplate-near-miss`, where they do not live.
findings.acceptance: Either the ge-1994 offsets-invariance check is added to the invariant suite so d/g are true as written, or d/g are corrected to describe the four committed cases exactly.
